items.description: PHP2Shell 漏洞在被披露前四天已遭黑客利用，Calif 与 Wiz 的研究人员发现这些漏洞。OpenAI 称其前沿 AI 在攻击者之前发现了漏洞，并与 PHP、Calif、Wiz 合作验证并开发补丁。NSA 建议无法立即更新的机构将系统离线，英国 NCSC 表示漏洞可能让黑客无需登录凭据即可控制网站服务器，白宫称联邦机构正在评估对政府系统和关键基础设施的潜在影响。  阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/m34xrhmqj1is6d1v1jna3ed46

items.title: OpenAI 发现 PHP「世纪漏洞」，全球 70% 网站都危险了

items.author: 彭海星
items.content: 两天前，代号 PHP2Shell 的两个 PHP 高危远程执行漏洞信息意外泄露，表明在最危险的情况下，攻击者可以通过 PHP 的漏洞，在服务器执行任意代码。 你可能听说过但不熟悉 PHP，但只需要知道， 全世界约有七成网站后台都使用了这项技术 ，使用比例高达 92% 的日本，更是成了「重灾区」。 于是，从昨晚开始，无数网站运维人员经历了夺命连环 call，高市早苗亲自发文敦促网站管理者打补丁，半个欧洲的政府与学术机构紧急「拔网线」，二次元熟悉的 niconico、pixiv，乃至《赛马娘》《碧蓝幻想》和任天堂相关游戏服务也纷纷下线，开始了归期未定的漫长升级。 想象你登录一个电商网站，下单买了一本书。这个过程中你看见的只是前端的网页，但服务器其实在后台处理了诸如验证密码、检查库存、查询订单、生成网页等动态功能。 根据统计，目前有 69.4% 的网站后端用到了 PHP，WordPress、Drupal、Joomla 等流行的网站管理系统都建立在 PHP 之上，维基百科使用的 MediaWiki，同样主要由 PHP 编写。 但就像曾经种满全球的大麦克香蕉被黄叶病团灭一样，普遍性本身也是一种脆弱性：如果 PHP 在底层上出现安全问题，可想而知，几乎全球的网站都会受到牵连。

items.title: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing

AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.”

Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. Meta is making a big push into AI, and it’s creating a new kind of stock that could help pay for it. On Wednesday, as the company reported its third-quarter earnings, Semafor reported the company might issue non-voting stock, meaning shares that don’t give their owners a vote on company decisions, to help fund its push into artificial intelligence. During Meta’s earnings call, the company confirmed that reporting. Meta’s chief financial officer, Susan Li, said the company plans to “create a new class of non-voting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders through a stock dividend.” Li later added that the company “created this new class of shares with the purpose of creating a publicly traded non-voting stock usable for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders.”

Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower. But it is how people are using it and how much they’re spending that has caught CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s attention. Zuckerberg said about 25% of people who set up Muse now use it daily, helping improve retention. He also shared that over a quarter of Muse’s engaged users who were shopping via the AI agent had an average purchase size of over $200, which was surprising even to industry insiders. “Plaid told us that they hadn’t seen activity like they’re seeing with their connector on any other service before,” Zuckerberg said, referring to the financial technology company that connects payment apps to customers’ bank accounts.
